paragraphs: EnergyCAP sells a utility bill management and energy management platform that it says has served organizations for over 40 years. The buyers are organizations with many buildings and utilities that need to track, audit, and manage bills across a portfolio. K-12 school districts are one of the named markets.

The platform collects detail from bills and meters covering electricity, natural gas, water, sewer, and other commodities. It is positioned as a single source of truth between meters and bills and a centralized system of record for utility expense management. The site claims customers identify billing errors in 1 in 5 bills. It integrates with ENERGY STAR. A Carbon Hub product acts as the central repository for carbon emissions data.

The company page traces the software to 1982, when it digitized manual energy management processes. In 2022 the company acquired an energy monitoring software business. The same timeline cites SOC 2 compliance and FedRAMP Certification. The company claims over 45 years of experience. The homepage puts its user count at 26,000 energy and utility professionals.

quote.text: EnergyCAP® brings energy, utility, and emissions data into one integrated platform
